summary: Carded from Fabio's ask: one supplied image in, a character sheet out, with the front full body HEADLESS. Not new on the board but never a card - it was candidate workflow 4 in MPI-348 s8, whose own working mode says surfaced ideas get their own card. Carries the Higgsfield HELL GRIND sheet spec (3 panels, headless front body, large 3/4 portrait, boring flat grey with no grain baked in, mandatory pupil catch-light, pick believable over beautiful) and flags that it CONFLICTS with Fabio's own best-performing layout from past tests (side + front profile + full body) - settle at the bench. Names the real risk: their sheets came from a PROMPT in a hosted creative model, ours must hold identity onto a back view from one photo, and MPI-348 s7 already records Qwen-Edit as weak on single-image instruction edits. Headless panel specced as a SAM3 mask + empty-prompt klein inpaint, not a prompt, which also honours their never-run-an-image-through-a-model-twice rule. Id claimed with exclusive mkdir.

Re-scoped by Fabio. The MPI-348 s8.4 layout (side + front profile + full body) is a LORA-TRAINING sheet - a different consumer - so the two layouts are NOT a conflict to settle; layout becomes a flow option keyed to purpose, and this card owns the VIDEO-REFERENCE layout only. Input is now TWO paths: attributes-only (what the character is, wardrobe, scars, age, hair colour, eye colour) restructured into the sheet prompt, and a reference photo. The attributes path is the LOW-RISK one and ships first - it is exactly what Higgsfield did (prompt to sheet in a hosted model) and has no identity-projection problem; the photo path keeps the unproven back-view step. Added: with structured fields a slot template needs no LLM, so Cubric Prompt earns its place only on free prose or per-model shaping. Recorded that their 'never write an age' rule does NOT transfer - that is a hosted content filter and Vision runs local models.

Two corrections from Fabio. (1) The LoRA-training sheet is OUT OF SCOPE, not a layout option - it is ~20 images and a whole different beast, addressed when that flow is addressed; MPI-504 owns the video-reference 3-panel sheet only. (2) The flow needs TWO MODELS, chosen per path at the bench - an EDIT model for the reference path, and for the attributes path whichever t2i model best obeys a prompt asking it to display the character in that layout. That second question is LAYOUT COMPLIANCE, not aesthetics, and has no answer on the board. Multiple models in one flow is the point of flows.

Re-scoped by Fabio to a SHIPPABLE v1: prompt-only, no image input. Krea2 t2i sheet from a proven prompt template, optional SAM3+Klein head removal on the small figure (default on), 8:5, 1k/2k (2k default), turbo off by default. In-graph enhancer recipe gets a character-only rewrite.
Ownership written to files.json: the card workspace plus the new raw flow graph candidate.

Re-scoped to a shippable v1 and retitled. Image input DROPPED to v2 (head-swap covers identity as a second pass), so the unproven back-view identity step leaves the card. Written this session with no GPU: plan.md (flow fields, the group-by-group strip of krea2_t2i_template.json, the SAM3+Klein head branch, five open bench calls) and prompts.md (the sheet template in four styles with the gendered words neutralised, the character-only enhancer system prompt for node 420, the removal prompt). Graph itself untouched - comfy_workflows/raw/ is user-owned.

Two decisions from Fabio. (1) GEAR POLICY settled: worn weapons/kit belong ON the sheet - the cowboy-movie sheets this layout comes from had none, and that cost separate item sheets plus unknown scale. Three tiers, all recipe text and NO new field: named gear always worn, at most two archetype-inevitable pieces when the user names none, none at all when the user rules it out in plain words. The third tier needs no UI because the LLM reads 'no weapons' as an instruction and the image prompt simply omits it - a negative never reaches Krea2, which is positive-phrasing-only. Hands stay open and empty; held objects remain banned. (2) HEAD PICKING solved by Fabio's face idea: a face exists only on the portrait and the FRONT body (the rear view has none), so detecting faces identifies the front panel with no classifier - retiring the left-half rectangle and keeping the rear view's hair reference. Verified against the engine source: SAM3_Detect sorts by CONFIDENCE not size (nodes_sam3.py:223 argsort on scores), so 'face number two' is a confidence race; sort by area with ImpactSEGSOrderedFilter instead. face_yolov8n.pt is already a shipped dep and emits SEGS directly. Also corrected the strip list: keep Input_Bypass_Filter_Lora, and the accelerator LoRA survives Detailer/Upscale deletion because Generation carries its own (440).

Enhancer regression run on bench 8188, no generation. Drafted recipe failed (in-prompt example returned verbatim for 2 of 4 inputs); revised to v3 over three arms. Positive-phrasing unfixable in the prompt on this 4B, closed with two RegexReplace scrub nodes verified offline. use_default_template measured inert.

flow_character_sheet.json created by stripping the seven groups from krea2_t2i_template.json: 218->82 nodes, 276->98 links, 10->3 groups, per-group counts asserted against plan.md before writing. Collapse worklist audited into plan.md.

Fabio cut the gear policy's THIRD TIER (user rules gear out -> sheet wears none). The regression disproved it: v1 gave 'a gunslinger, no weapons' a gunbelt outright, and v3 only read clean because the model NAMED the absences and the scrub deleted the naming - phrasing luck, not compliance. Recipe rule 5 deleted and rules renumbered; recipe now writes the character only. Gear exclusion becomes the user's job via a PROMPT REVIEW step, which is not new architecture: it is the shipped Describe Image shape (op declares outputKind text, graph carries the Output_prompt PreviewAny - node 242 already exists here, generationService branches on outputKind before the empty-media check, describeAction emits workspace:inject-prompts so the text lands in the prompt box editable). Optional button, not the default path; wired in the /mpi-add-flow pass. The two RegexReplace scrub nodes STAY - negation is not weapons-specific ('no facial hair', 'no tattoos') and reaches Krea2 the same way. Rejected: a StringContains-triggered weapon-clause regex, an open-ended wordlist that would also delete a wanted satchel. Regression input 4 demoted from gate to watch: it must still prove the user's words 'no weapons' never survive into the output.

STRIP LIST RETIRED - it deletes load-bearing nodes and fails silently. Traced in the file: the Edit group BUILDS the shared conditioning (51/282 CLIPTextEncode off Get_positive/negative text, 294/302 MpiIfElse plain-vs-grounded, 143/290 ToBasicPipe High/Balanced, 621 MpiIfElse on Get_turbo -> 253 Set_Models), and 77 FromBasicPipe inside the KEPT Generation group reads Get_Models - so deleting Edit costs every sampler its positive, negative and vae. The Images group holds 75 Input_Width / 74 Input_Height -> 458 Set_W / 459 Set_H -> 560 EmptyLatentImage, so deleting it costs the fixed 8:5 resolution. SetNode/GetNode link by NAME, so a link-integrity check passes on a decapitated graph - which is why the earlier 'all links resolve: true' meant nothing. The 50-node intermediate was removed; krea2_t2i_template.json untouched throughout. FABIO'S CALL: he strips it in the bench editor (t2i only), and prompt enhancement becomes its own workflow flow_character_enhance.json - ~10 nodes, no UNET/VAE/sampler, the shipped image_descriptor.json shape. Consequences: the sheet graph drops the whole Prompt Enhancement group and node 241, Input_enhance_prompt disappears as a field (the button enhances, the box holds the result, the sheet takes it verbatim, so double-enhance is impossible), and Output_prompt is rewired to the ASSEMBLED sheet prompt so the MPI-242 record is what Krea2 actually saw. Keep-list and enhancer spec in plan.md. Also v4 recipe (rule 5 removed) confirmed on the bench: 70-82 words 4/4, no example leak, nothing held 4/4, scrub clean 4/4. Input 4 returned 'with a gunbelt slung low across his hips' - positively phrased, uncatchable by any scrub, which is the empirical proof that cutting tier 3 was correct.

Fabio exported two hand-built graphs; both verified offline, no generation. krea2_t2i_only.json (54 nodes) is CLEAN - 0 orphan Gets, 0 dangling required inputs, all links resolve, conditioning intact via FromBasicPipe<-Get_Models, resolution wired direct from Input_Width/Input_Height, Input_Bypass_Filter_Lora still at strength 1, both turbo switches live (621 picks the Balanced/High pipe, 619 picks the decode), four samplers 25/8/3/2, zero TextGenerate. Fixed on his explicit authorisation: node 665 title Input_height -> Input_Height (single token, 54 nodes/69 links unchanged) - the app canonical is capital H and the lowercase form appears nowhere in js/, so injection would have silently missed it. LoRA rack KEPT by Fabio as a feature: a user with a character LoRA loads it and describes only wardrobe/hair/face on top - LoRA carries identity, sheet carries layout. Needs no new machinery; flow_ltx_extend and flow_ltx_foley already ship the same six-slot rack and comfyController routes Input_Lora_N through its MPI-219 LoRA-object branch. qwen3vl_4b_prompt_enhancer.json (10 nodes) has the right skeleton and exact sampler params but THREE OPEN GAPS: its system prompt is still the OLD scene-writing recipe (node 420 never swapped, 2137 chars vs v4 3885, 28 v4 lines absent), both RegexReplace scrub nodes are missing, and Input_enhance_prompt defaults to false so as exported it returns the users raw text unchanged - delete that MpiIfElse rather than flipping it.

Patched qwen3vl_4b_prompt_enhancer.json directly, on Fabio's go, to avoid hand-transcribing a 3885-char prompt and two escaped regexes. (1) System prompt swapped from the OLD scene-writing recipe to v4, read out of prompts.md and confirmed byte-for-byte identical after the round trip (2137 -> 3885 chars). (2) Two RegexReplace nodes inserted between StringReplace and Output_prompt, shaped like the StringReplace already in the graph - three widget values only, so case_insensitive (true), multiline/dotall (false) and count (0) take their defaults, which are the wanted values; no RegexReplace existed anywhere in the repo to copy, so the shape was derived from /object_info. (3) The Input_enhance_prompt MpiIfElse was DELETED rather than flipped from false - the workflow only ever enhances and a toggle that can make it a passthrough is a footgun. Result: 11 nodes, 10 links, no dangling required inputs, all links resolve, ChatML branch untouched, chain is CLIPLoader -> TextGenerate -> StringReplace -> scrub-negation -> tidy -> Output_prompt. Both patterns survive the JSON round trip byte for byte and, applied AS STORED to the four real v4 outputs, give 61-71 words with no negation and no trailing stop 4/4. Still unproven: that Python re agrees with the offline JS check - needs one live run, not yet authorised.

Fabio: the Image Descriptor already drives this same 4B, so the enhancer must be UNIVERSAL with the recipe injected at run time. Done, and it needed retitles rather than new plumbing - _inject sprays into value/string and MPI-359's Title.widget form addresses one named widget. Inject keys: Input_System_Prompt (the recipe), Input_Positive (user text), Input_Scrub_Negation.regex_pattern and Input_Tidy.regex_pattern. The scrub patterns were made injectable too, deliberately: a universal workflow with a baked character-sheet scrub would silently mangle another flow's output, and a flow that wants none injects a pattern that cannot match ((?!x)x, verified live - the trailing full stop survives, proving the injected pattern replaced the baked one). Character-sheet values remain the baked defaults so it runs standalone at the bench. Also added MpiClearVram after TextGenerate, where image_descriptor.json puts it, since the 4B stays resident and a sheet generation usually follows. 12 nodes, 11 links, converts cleanly through scripts/workflow-to-api.mjs with _meta.title intact. LIVE PROOF, two arms, no image: defaults gave 61-71 words with no negation and no trailing stop on all four inputs, each matching the offline JS scrub prediction BYTE FOR BYTE (so Python re agrees with JS), with execution_cached covering only [7,9] so TextGenerate ran fresh; and an injected translator recipe returned French. Consequence for the docs: the recipe is now APP payload, not graph payload - prompts.md's opening claim was corrected. Open for /mpi-add-flow: whether the op should be a universal promptEnhance in the getUniversalWorkflow('imageDescribe') shape rather than sheet-specific.

Wired the sheet prompt into comfy_workflows/raw/krea2_t2i_only.json on Fabio's explicit authorisation (raw/ is user-owned). 54 -> 62 nodes, 69 -> 77 links. Four PrimitiveStringMultiline recipes 666-669 -> 670 MpiAnySwitch Recipe_Select, select <- 671 MpiInt Input_Recipe - RENAMED from Input_Style by Fabio so the bank-behind-an-int generalises to any later flow, and so it stays clear of Input_Style_Selector, which is the style-LoRA rack. 672 StringReplace Sheet_Prompt: find [CHARACTER PROMPT], string <- 670, replace <- 112 Input_Positive VERBATIM; output feeds 658 Set_positive text (old link 1386 deleted) and 673 PreviewAny Output_prompt, so what the app records is the ASSEMBLED prompt Krea2 saw (MPI-242 contract). The three non-photoreal templates were GENERATED from the one skeleton in prompts.md s1 rather than transcribed, with the generated Photoreal asserted byte-identical to the canonical block there (1417 chars). Verified offline, no generation: link integrity clean; 0 orphan Gets (the single unread Set_model 529 predates the edit, confirmed against the pre-patch copy); 62 of 62 nodes reachable upstream from SaveImage / Output_Image / Output_prompt with Get->Set as an edge; substitution simulated for all four recipes (241-246 words); workflow-to-api.mjs exit 0 against the live bench with _meta.title intact and 51 CLIPTextEncode.text <- 672; all 16 injectable titles unique; 671 presents an unwired int key, which _inject sprays (comfyController.js:1373), the same path Input_Width uses. Nothing generated - no sheet image exists. FIRST SHEET GENERATED and the layout PASSES. One run on bench 8188 under the new GPU lease, prompt_id ff505256, 40.0s, status success, execution_cached only [69]. Rig is 1280x768 with turbo ON, seed 504504, Photoreal recipe - Fabio's call that 1k+turbo is the correct test since placement is what matters and the sheet feeds another model, so 2k turbo-off would cost time and prove nothing. Input_Positive was a hand-written v4-shape phrase; the enhancer is already proven and was not in the loop. RESULT: two narrow equal-width full bodies on the left (one front, one from directly behind) and a large 3/4 head-and-shoulders portrait filling the right, one continuous grey backdrop across all three, flat even light, no grain; wardrobe consistent across panels (fringed buckskin coat, red trade shirt, brass-buckle belt with sheathed knife at the right hip, fringed moccasin boots); scar on the left cheekbone, clean-shaven, catch-light in both pupils. 673 Output_prompt returned the ASSEMBLED 303-word prompt as node text, so the MPI-242 contract is proven LIVE rather than only through the converter. ONE REAL DEVIATION: the rear panel's hair drifts - brown and wavy against straight iron-grey on the front body and the portrait, while face and wardrobe hold. That is the axis the sheet exists to lock, so it is the next bench item: wording first (the template's rear clause names how the hair falls, not its colour), then a seed sweep to separate systematic from unlucky. Observations, no action: 442 SaveImage is mode 4 (bypassed) in the hand-stripped graph so only 494 Output_Image emits, and the output is a ComfyUI temp file that dies on bench restart - the fixed seed reproduces it. Head-removal branch still does not exist, so the front body still has its head; nothing in the app is wired.

Rear-panel hair drift A/B, two arms at 1280x768 turbo ON under one GPU lease (queued behind another agent's hold). ARM C, control wording verbatim on a fresh seed 777001: same dark brown wavy rear panel - so the drift is SYSTEMATIC, not seed luck. ARM B, rear clause changed to 'the same straight iron-grey hair falling between the shoulder blades' at the SAME seed 504504 as run 1: rear panel moved from dark brown to grey-streaked, so the description does reach that panel - but 'straight' did nothing and the rear hair stayed wavy in all three runs. Conclusion: colour responds to the wording, texture does not, and the wording knob is real but partial. Everything else held on both arms - layout, continuous backdrop, wardrobe, knife at the right hip, catch-light. One-sample watch item: arm C's portrait came back closer to straight-on than the requested ~30 degrees. This is not cosmetic: the front body's head is removed by the Klein pass, so the rear panel is the only hair-from-behind reference the video model ever gets. NEXT ARM PROPOSED, NOT RUN: name hair colour and texture in the TEMPLATE's global identity clause ('the same character in every view with identical face, hair and wardrobe'), which governs all three panels, rather than leaning harder on the character phrase, which has shown its ceiling. Template payload, no graph change.

Arm D NEGATIVE. One run, 1280x768 turbo ON, character phrase and seed held at run 1 (504504), 35.1s success; only the sheet template changed, and only in the API payload - raw/ was not touched. The clause tested was character-agnostic on purpose: 'the same character in every view with identical face, hair and wardrobe' -> '... identical face and wardrobe, and identical hair colour, hair length and hair texture in all three views'. The rear panel came back dark brown and wavy, indistinguishable from the control. Ranked at the held seed: arm B (colour named in the CHARACTER phrase's rear clause) grey-streaked = best; run 1 control and arm D both dark brown. SETTLED: the knob is the character phrase's rear clause, not the template - Krea2 attends to concrete rear-view description and ignores a general all-views-must-match instruction, which matches how the rest of this prompt carries the layout. Consequence: the fix is enhancer-recipe payload, the template stays as Fabio wrote it, and the graph does not move. Hair TEXTURE responded to nothing - wavy at the back across three seeds and two clause positions, including an arm that said 'straight' outright - so it is recorded as a known v1 limitation rather than chased, to be revisited at the 10/10 stress test. Written to prompts.md s2 as a PROPOSED v4.1 amendment to recipe rule 4 (restate the hair colour in the rear clause itself), explicitly NOT applied to the recipe text and NOT yet regressed - the v4 regression was run against the current wording, so the amendment needs its own text-only pass first.

CORRECTION plus a decision. Fabio asked what the hair work was actually chasing, which exposed two conflated defects. COLOUR: the character phrase stated 'long iron-grey hair' and the rear panel rendered brown on two seeds - a real adherence failure on a stated attribute. TEXTURE: the phrase never asked for straight or wavy at all, so a wavy back view violated no instruction; the actual defect is that the panels disagree with each other, which is what matters for a reference sheet whichever texture is picked. The earlier write-up that 'texture does not respond to wording' is WITHDRAWN as never established - arm B put 'straight' in the REAR clause only while the main hair clause named no texture, so the attribute was never stated where every panel reads it; a patch was tested and a conclusion drawn about the mechanism. FABIO'S CALL: name the hair ONCE, in full - colour and texture together in the main clause, the rear clause naming only how it falls or is tied, no attribute repeated, on the reading that saying the same thing twice is what confuses the model. This REVERSES the proposed v4.1 amendment (rear clause restates the colour), which stays in prompts.md s2 as the record of what arm B measured but is now marked superseded and unadopted - noted honestly against Fabio's reading, arm B did measure better BY repeating, so the two predictions differ and one run separates them. NEXT ARM, UNRUN: 'long straight iron-grey hair worn loose past the shoulders' in the MAIN clause, rear clause untouched, seed 504504 held for direct comparison against run 1, B and D. Panels agree = description gap and the recipe takes the single-mention shape; panels still disagree = texture consistency is a model limit, established on evidence rather than assumed.

Arms E and F: the single-mention hair shape is NEGATIVE and Fabio's reading is disconfirmed. ARM E, Fabio's call - colour AND texture together in the MAIN clause ('long straight iron-grey hair worn loose past the shoulders'), rear clause left exactly as run 1 with nothing repeated, seed 504504 held, 1280x768 turbo ON, 45.1s, execution_cached empty: the rear panel came back at saturation 0.181 against the control's 0.182 - no movement at all. ARM F then ran the one cell nobody had tried, arm E's full main clause AND arm B's rear repeat together, same seed, 36.1s, cached only loaders and constants so it executed fresh: 0.165. That makes the two REPEATING arms (B 0.161, F 0.165) the only two that have ever moved the rear panel, against a 0.181-0.184 control band - so repetition is mildly helpful, not the source of the confusion. The v4.1 rear-clause repeat in prompts.md s2 is REINSTATED as the best-measured shape with arm F its strongest form, but NOT adopted: it reverses Fabio's explicit call and needs his go, and raw/ is untouched. SECOND RESULT: rear-view texture IS a model limit and is now established rather than assumed - 'straight' has been stated in the main clause, the rear clause, both at once and in the template, and the rear view came back wavy in all six runs across three seeds while the portrait renders long straight iron-grey hair correctly in the same frame. Effect size of any wording is ~0.02 saturation against a ~0.05-0.07 rear-to-portrait gap: the best arm narrows the disagreement, nothing closes it. MEASUREMENT CORRECTION worth keeping: the first metric sampled the darkest 30 percent of a head box, which is SHADOW not hair, and reported the grey front-body hair as MORE saturated than the brown rear hair - backwards. The numbers above come from hair-only boxes restricted to mid-tone pixels (luminance 45-170); the front-body head is only ~70px tall and its box catches collar and skin at some seeds, so front-body numbers are untrustworthy at 1k and the rear-vs-portrait pair is what carries the weight. PROCESS: all four earlier arms had to be rebuilt from the bench's /history because only their outcomes were ever written down, and that history dies on a bench restart - every arm's character phrase is now recorded verbatim in validation.md. NOTE ON THE STAMP: this event's 'at' is real time read from the clock and cross-checked against GitHub's Date header (both 2026-08-19T11:58Z, VPN off, no skew), so it sits EARLIER than the hand-authored 13:10Z stamp above it. Ordering is append order, as this card already documents.

Fabio ADOPTED the arm F hair shape (his single-mention call was an observation carried from other models, not a verdict) and asked to keep testing wording. Recipe categories 2 and 4 in prompts.md s2 now carry it, making the recipe v4.1 and owing a text-only regression pass. Six more arms ran at seed 504504: G (a concrete PANEL-LOCAL template clause on the rear view) NEGATIVE, I (poker-straight) NEGATIVE, K (worn loose -> hanging straight down) apparently the best yet at rear sat 0.144, and L/M/N filling in a tidy dose-response between F and K. THEN FABIO ASKED WHETHER THESE HAD RUN ON ONE SEED OR SEVERAL, AND THAT INVALIDATED THE RANKING. Every arm was n=1 at seed 504504. A six-run noise floor - F and K at 777001, 123123 and 909090 - came out 2-2 on per-seed wins, with the within-arm range (-0.119 to 0.103 on the rear-to-portrait gap) an order of magnitude wider than the between-arm mean difference (0.009 vs 0.014). K's win is WITHDRAWN and so is the whole G/I/K/L/M/N ranking. The metric does not survive a seed change either: composition shifts move the fixed sample boxes, and F123123's portrait box landed on the red shirt (sat 0.289), which is why that gap went negative - only WITHIN-seed comparisons are valid and the visual verdict is what carries across seeds. Also noted: holding the seed never made wording the only variable, because editing the prompt changes the conditioning and the sampler takes a different path, so same-seed-different-prompt is a fresh draw. WHAT SURVIVED, and it is the useful half: the F shape fixes rear-panel COLOUR and it REPLICATES - at 777001 the control renders the rear brown and F renders it grey, same at 909090 and 123123. Seed 504504 is an unusually hard seed and it is the only one the investigation ever used, which made a solved problem look unsolved for eleven arms. Rear-view TEXTURE stays wavy at every seed under every wording while the portrait renders it straight in the same frame: a model limit, now on four seeds rather than one. That claim has now been stated, withdrawn, re-established on arm K and withdrawn again when K failed to reproduce - both flips caused by n=1 at one seed. DEAD LEVERS, do not retest: the sheet template (arm D global clause and arm G panel-local clause, both no-ops), the negative prompt at 1k turbo (nodes 72 and 162 are cfg 1.0 so Input_Negative is inert; only the quality path 311 at cfg 2.0 makes it live), and stronger texture words. STANDING RULE for this flow: one seed is a pilot, not a result - wording verdicts need 3-4 seeds compared per seed. Last untested mechanism for texture is RESOLUTION (does the rear hair resolve straighter at 2k than at 1k), which is not a wording question.

THE REAR-HAIR DEFECT WAS THE TEST RIG. A 2x2 grid, three seeds per cell, F wording: turbo ON renders the rear hair wavy at BOTH 1k and 2k, turbo OFF renders it straight at BOTH. The 2k-turbo cell settles it - same resolution as the fix, same defect as the rig. Resolution is irrelevant to hair texture; the sampler path is the whole effect (72/162 at 8+3 steps cfg 1.0 vs 311/436 at 25+2 cfg 2.0) and it reproduces at 1k, so it costs 111s to test rather than 328s. Eleven wording arms chased an artefact of the rig; the 1k+turbo rig was right for placement, which is what it was chosen for, and nothing before this grid could have shown it invalid for texture. SEAMS at 2k-quality (the sheet splits into three plates where turbo keeps one continuous backdrop) are ACCEPTED by Fabio, not a defect - the sheets still work as a reference, so that spec line is a preference not a gate. ANIME/CYBERPUNK, nine runs, Recipe_Anime across three rigs x three seeds: 2k-turbo is the best sheet this card has produced - crisp cel line art, continuous backdrop, every garment and gear item consistent, circuit motif on the jacket back, rear hair straight black with pink ends, catch-lights present - AND THE TURBO WAVE ARTEFACT DOES NOT APPEAR THERE, so it is not universal. 2k-quality anime is WORSE: sketchy concept-sketch line art and the rear panel put the HOOD UP, hiding the hair entirely, which is a functional failure for a reference sheet. The ~105-word phrase overran the recipe's own 90-word ceiling with no failure, a null result in favour of open call #4. RIG POLICY (Fabio): realistic -> turbo OFF + 2k; stylised -> turbo ON; both controls stay user-facing because low-VRAM users need the choice. TURBO LOCKS THE CHARACTER, NON-TURBO VARIES IT - Fabio's observation, confirmed on this card's own runs: photoreal F wording at three seeds gives the SAME man under turbo and three visibly DIFFERENT men without it, so non-turbo is a VARIATION lever for hunting a face, not merely a quality setting. That also partly explains the small between-arm wording deltas - every arm ran under turbo, against a locked character. HEAD BRANCH REVISED (Fabio): stage 1 is UNCHANGED and still required - face_yolov8n plus the ordered filter still SELECT which head is operated on, and that picked region is the area to inpaint - but the mask that gets filled is a UNION OF THREE SAM3 SEMANTIC MASKS, hair + face + hat. What is retired is the face's grown bbox used AS the mask. Reasons from experience: a face-only mask fails on a hatted character (measured on the cowboy-movie work, where inpainting a face under a hat required the hat in the mask), hair falling over clothing needs a precise hair mask, and a box stamped on the head makes the inpaint model destroy the clothing detail it covers and invent new detail in its place. Open: the no-hat case must degrade to hair+face without the empty detection zeroing the union, and the hair/face/hat -> SAM3 text-branch mapping is an inference to confirm at the bench.

note: v4.1 recipe regression ran: 24 samples, 3 arms x 2 seeds. Four v3 guarantees hold. Category 4 was ignored 6/8 - slot template (v4.2) fixed rear colour 2/8 -> 8/8 and is now shipped. v4.3 disproved (instruction example leaked).
